input.question: Why are electric cars less taxing on the environment than standard fuel-burning cars, if we still require fossil fuels to make the electricity for the cars?
input.ground_truth: 1) Like you mentioned, the source of electricity can come from renewable sources. And depending on where you are, it can be significant. Where I live, Wind, Nuclear, and Hydro make up 60% of the electricity in my province. With natural gas making up the other 30% and coal 10%. So instantly there's a 60% reduction in carbon emissions. 2) Due to the size and type of fuel in a car engine, car engines are not as efficient as electricity generation. Car engines are constrained to be light and small, so that reduces the efficiency they have. Generating electricity in a power plant, even if it's using fossil fuels, is more fuel efficient than the efficiencies gained in a car engine.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are electric cars less taxing on the environment than standard fuel-burning cars, if we still require fossil fuels to make the electricity for the cars?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two ways to make your toy car go zoom.

One way is to use a little fire inside the car that burns "coal" or "gas" to make it move. When that fire burns, it makes a lot of yucky smoke that goes into the air and can make the air dirty and the Earth warm.

The other way is to plug your toy car into a big wall outlet (or a special charging station) and use electricity to make it go zoom. The electricity might come from a power plant that still burns some coal or gas to make the electricity—but here’s the cool part: those big power plants can also use cleaner things like wind, sun, or water to make electricity, and they can do it in a way that makes less yucky smoke than lots of little car engines all over the place.

Also, when a big power plant makes electricity, it can be done more efficiently than when a tiny engine in a car tries to make power. That means less "waste" and less yucky stuff going into the air for every mile you drive.

So, even though making electricity might still use some fossil fuels, using electric cars means we can make the air cleaner overall, especially if we use more clean electricity in the future!
